title: Use your microphone over remote desktop on a Mac
shortTitle: Your microphone on a remote Mac
metaDescription: Remote desktop tools send a Mac's screen, not your voice. How to use your microphone, camera and speaker in web meetings on a Mac you control remotely.
keywords: use microphone over remote desktop mac
markdown:
Remote desktop tools send the Mac's screen, keyboard and mouse to you. None of the common ones send your microphone to a Mac: there is no microphone passthrough to a Mac host. To talk in a meeting that runs on the remote Mac, keep your remote desktop tool (Parsec, AnyDesk, TeamViewer, Screen Sharing, Chrome Remote Desktop or another) for the screen and run Remote Visio beside it: it turns the browser on the device in front of you into the microphone, camera and speaker of that Mac, for meetings held in its browser.

## Why your microphone does not reach the Mac

Microphone redirection exists, but mostly in one direction. Microsoft's Remote Desktop (RDP) redirects your microphone when the far end is a Windows PC. When the far end is a Mac, the usual tools stop at the screen. This is how they behave when the controlled computer is a Mac, as tested by Remote Visio's author:

| Tool | Screen and input | Your microphone |
|---|---|---|
| TeamViewer | Yes | No, it picks up the Mac's own microphone instead |
| AnyDesk | Yes | No |
| Parsec | Yes | No |
| RustDesk | Yes | No |
| Jump Desktop | Yes | No |
| ToDesk | Yes | No: it has microphone mapping, but the controlled end must be Windows |
| macOS Screen Sharing | Yes | No |
| Microsoft RDP (far end is Windows) | Yes | Yes, built in, and it stops at Windows |

So you open Google Meet on the remote Mac, you can see everyone, and nobody can hear you.

## What Remote Visio does

Remote Visio has two parts on the Mac and none on your side:

- **The Remote Visio app** sits in the Mac's menu bar. It serves a web page, the *sender page*, at `https://<your Mac>:7420`, and receives your microphone and camera from it over an encrypted peer-to-peer WebRTC connection.
- **The Remote Visio browser extension**, for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc and other Chromium browsers, gives web pages on the Mac three more devices: **Remote Visio Microphone**, **Remote Visio Speaker** and **Remote Visio Camera**. A meeting picks them like any other device.

On the device in front of you (a laptop, a phone, a tablet), you only open the sender page in a browser. What the meeting plays into Remote Visio Speaker comes back to that page, so you hear the meeting too.

## What you need

- The remote Mac: macOS 14.2 or later. The installer is for Apple Silicon; an Intel Mac builds Remote Visio from source.
- A Chromium browser on that Mac (version 111 or later), where your meetings run.
- A browser with a microphone on the device in front of you.
- A network path between the two: the same local network, or [Tailscale](/guides/tailscale-setup-for-remote-visio) on both (free).
- Your usual remote desktop tool, for the screen.

## Set it up

1. **Connect the two devices.** If they are not on the same local network, install Tailscale on both and sign in with the same account. The sending device must reach port 7420 on the Mac.
2. **Install Remote Visio on the Mac.** [Download the installer](/download) and run it. The app starts, sits in the menu bar and starts at login from then on.
3. **Add the browser extension.** In the menu-bar menu, choose **Install Browser Extension…**. It opens the extension's Chrome Web Store page in your browser: click **Add to Chrome** (**Get** in Edge), then pin the extension so its button stays in the toolbar. Reload meeting pages that were already open.
4. **Open the sender page on your device.** The menu-bar menu lists the Mac's addresses. Open one, for example `https://100.101.102.103:7420`, accept the certificate warning once (a tool on your own network cannot get a publicly trusted certificate) and press **Start**. Allow the microphone, and the camera if you want to send video.
5. **Pick the devices in the meeting.** In the meeting's settings on the Mac, choose Remote Visio Microphone, Remote Visio Speaker and Remote Visio Camera, then click **Allow** when the extension asks whether the site may use them. It asks once per site.
6. **Turn off audio in your remote desktop tool.** Remote Visio now carries the meeting's sound back to you. If the remote tool still forwards sound, you hear the meeting twice.

On the sender page, each device shows a status: green when it gets through and a meeting uses it, amber while it is on its way, red with what to fix.

## Limits to know first

- **Web meetings only, for the microphone and the speaker.** They exist in web pages of a Chromium browser on the Mac. The Zoom, Teams and FaceTime apps, macOS dictation, Safari and Firefox cannot see them. Join from the browser instead: see [Join Zoom and Teams meetings from the browser](/guides/join-zoom-teams-from-browser-on-mac).
- **The camera can go further.** Builds that include the optional Remote Visio Camera system extension give video apps a virtual camera too, after a one-time approval in System Settings.
- **No pairing code yet.** Anyone who can reach port 7420 on your Mac, or a web page open on a device that can, can connect as the sender. Keep it on networks you trust, such as your own tailnet.
- **Latency is about a phone call's.** Fine for talking and meetings, not for monitoring yourself while recording music.

## A Mac mini at home, or a Mac in a rack

The setup is the same for any Mac you reach from far away, whether it sits in another room, at the office or in a rack. What matters is that you can install apps on it, that it runs a Chromium browser for the meetings, and that your device can reach it, which Tailscale usually solves. If the Mac is in the same room as an iPhone, you probably do not need Remote Visio: Apple's Continuity Microphone already does that.

Ready to try it? [Download Remote Visio for Mac](/download), then [add the extension](/extension).

title: Parsec with a Mac host: getting your microphone into meetings
metaDescription: Parsec shows you a Mac host's screen but does not send your microphone to it. How to talk in web meetings on the Mac by running Remote Visio beside Parsec.
markdown:
Parsec gives you a Mac host's screen, keyboard and mouse, but it has no microphone passthrough to a Mac host: your microphone does not reach the Mac. To speak in a meeting that runs on the Mac, keep Parsec for the picture and run Remote Visio next to it: Remote Visio carries your microphone, your camera and the meeting's sound on a separate connection, and Parsec does not need to know.

## What Parsec does, and what it leaves out

Parsec is built for responsive remote control, and it does that part well on a Mac host. What it does not do, when the host is a Mac, is make your microphone available to the Mac's apps. That is true of the other common remote desktop tools as well: TeamViewer, AnyDesk, RustDesk, Jump Desktop and macOS Screen Sharing. (This is based on how each tool behaves with a Mac host, as tested by Remote Visio's author. Tools change; if yours has added it, you may not need anything else.)

The result is familiar: you join Google Meet or Teams on the Mac through Parsec, you see the call, and nobody can hear you.

## How Remote Visio fits next to Parsec

Remote Visio is not a remote desktop tool. It has a menu-bar app on the Mac and a browser extension in a Chromium browser there. On the device you sit at, you open one web page:

- **Parsec** keeps carrying the screen, keyboard and mouse.
- **Remote Visio** carries your microphone and camera to the Mac, and the meeting's sound back to you, over an encrypted peer-to-peer WebRTC connection.

On the Mac, the meeting picks **Remote Visio Microphone**, **Remote Visio Speaker** and **Remote Visio Camera** like any other device.

## Setup, step by step

1. **Make sure your device can reach the Mac.** Parsec has its own way of connecting; Remote Visio needs your device to reach port 7420 on the Mac directly. On the same local network that already works. From elsewhere, install Tailscale on both and sign in with the same account (see the [Tailscale guide](/guides/tailscale-setup-for-remote-visio)).
2. **Install Remote Visio on the Mac**, through your Parsec session: [download the installer](/download) and run it. The app appears in the menu bar.
3. **Add the [browser extension](/extension)** from the menu-bar menu: **Install Browser Extension…**, then **Add to Chrome** on the store page, and pin it.
4. **On your own computer**, open the Mac's address in a browser, for example `https://100.101.102.103:7420` (the menu-bar menu lists the addresses). Accept the certificate warning once and press **Start**.
5. **In the meeting on the Mac**, choose Remote Visio Microphone and Remote Visio Speaker (and Remote Visio Camera if you send video), and allow the site once.

## Turn off the remote tool's sound

Remote Visio sends what the meeting plays into Remote Visio Speaker back to your browser, on its own low-latency connection. If your remote desktop tool also plays the Mac's sound to you, you will hear the meeting twice, with two different delays. Turn sound off in the remote tool's settings and leave the meeting's sound to Remote Visio. The [echo guide](/guides/fix-echo-remote-desktop-meetings) covers the other symptoms.

Keep the sender page's speaker on while you talk: while it is on, your browser's echo cancellation is on too, so the meeting coming out of your speakers is not sent back into it.

## What to expect

- **Latency** is roughly a phone call's: the network's delay plus a small buffer that the Mac's browser sizes to the network. Fine for meetings.
- **Two connections** run side by side, Parsec's and Remote Visio's. They do not interfere: Remote Visio does not touch the screen, and Parsec does not touch Remote Visio's audio.
- **Meetings in the browser.** The microphone and speaker exist in web pages of a Chromium browser on the Mac (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Vivaldi, Opera). The Zoom and Teams apps cannot see them: join those meetings from the browser. See [Join Zoom and Teams from the browser](/guides/join-zoom-teams-from-browser-on-mac).
- **Room noise.** If the Mac stands in a room with people or a TV, its menu has **Controls → Mute This Mac's Microphone** and **Mute This Mac's Speakers**, so the room stays out of the meeting while Remote Visio runs.

## Troubleshooting in one minute

- *The meeting hears nothing.* On the sender page, the microphone's status must be green and its meter must move when you talk. In the meeting's settings, Remote Visio Microphone must be selected.
- *Remote Visio's devices are missing from the meeting.* Reload the meeting page after installing the extension, and check that the meeting runs in the Chromium browser profile where the extension is installed.
- *The page will not load on your computer.* Port 7420 is not reachable: check that both devices are on Tailscale or the same network.

More on the [support page](/support). Ready? [Download Remote Visio for Mac](/download).

title: AnyDesk, TeamViewer and Screen Sharing: talk in a meeting on the remote Mac
seoTitle: AnyDesk, TeamViewer, Screen Sharing: your mic on a Mac
metaDescription: AnyDesk, TeamViewer and macOS Screen Sharing do not send your microphone to a Mac. One fix works with all of them, and other remote tools: Remote Visio.
markdown:
AnyDesk, TeamViewer and macOS Screen Sharing all let you control a Mac from somewhere else. None of them sends your microphone to that Mac, so a meeting you join there cannot hear you. The fix is the same for all three, and for other remote desktop tools such as Chrome Remote Desktop: keep the tool for the screen, and let Remote Visio carry your microphone, camera and the meeting's sound.

## Tool by tool

These notes describe each tool's behaviour when the controlled computer is a Mac, as tested by Remote Visio's author. Tools change; if yours has added microphone forwarding to Macs, you may not need anything else.

### AnyDesk

AnyDesk forwards the Mac's screen and your keyboard and mouse. Your microphone does not reach the Mac's apps. Meetings on the Mac see only the Mac's own microphones, if it has any.

### TeamViewer

TeamViewer does not send your microphone to a Mac either: it picks up **the Mac's own microphone** instead. That is the room the Mac stands in, not you. If that room is an office, the meeting hears the office.

### macOS Screen Sharing

Apple's Screen Sharing gives you the Mac's screen and control of it. It has no setting that turns your microphone into a microphone of the remote Mac.

### Other tools

The same applies to RustDesk, Jump Desktop and Parsec ([Parsec guide](/guides/parsec-microphone-mac-host)), and ToDesk maps the microphone only when the controlled computer runs Windows. Remote Visio does not depend on your remote tool, so it works the same next to Chrome Remote Desktop or any other.

## The common fix

Remote Visio runs on the Mac (a menu-bar app plus a browser extension) and in a browser on your side. It gives web meetings on the Mac three devices, **Remote Visio Microphone**, **Remote Visio Speaker** and **Remote Visio Camera**, fed by the device in front of you over an encrypted peer-to-peer WebRTC connection.

1. **Network.** Your device must reach port 7420 on the Mac: the same local network, or [Tailscale](/guides/tailscale-setup-for-remote-visio) on both.
2. **Install** Remote Visio on the Mac through your remote session: [download it](/download), run the installer.
3. **Add the [browser extension](/extension)** from the menu-bar menu (**Install Browser Extension…**) and pin it.
4. **Open the sender page** on your device: `https://<the Mac's address>:7420`, accept the certificate once, press **Start**, allow the microphone and the camera.
5. **In the meeting on the Mac**, pick the three Remote Visio devices and allow the site once.
6. **Turn the remote tool's sound off**, so you hear the meeting once, through Remote Visio.

## Keep the room out: mute the Mac's own microphone

With TeamViewer in particular, the Mac's own microphone has been the meeting's input until now. Once Remote Visio Microphone is selected, the meeting hears you instead. If you also want to be sure nothing in the room gets in (another app, another tab, a page that picked the built-in microphone by name), use the menu-bar menu: **Controls → Mute This Mac's Microphone**. It mutes the Mac's own microphones, built-in, USB and Bluetooth, while Remote Visio runs, and puts them back when it stops. Remote Visio Microphone is not affected.

**Mute This Mac's Speakers** does the same for the Mac's outputs, so alerts and other tabs do not play in the room. What the meeting sends to Remote Visio Speaker still reaches you.

## Limits

- The microphone and the speaker work in **web pages of a Chromium browser** on the Mac: Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Vivaldi, Opera. The Zoom, Teams and FaceTime apps, Safari and Firefox do not see them. [Join from the browser](/guides/join-zoom-teams-from-browser-on-mac).
- Anyone who can reach port 7420 on the Mac, or a web page open on a device that can, can connect as the sender: there is no pairing code in this version. Keep the port inside your local network or tailnet.
- An iPhone in the same room as the Mac does not need any of this: Apple's Continuity Microphone is free.

## If something does not work

- *Nobody hears you:* the sender page's microphone status should be green and say a page on the Mac uses it. If it is amber with "no meeting uses Remote Visio Microphone yet", pick it in the meeting's audio settings.
- *You hear yourself, or the meeting twice:* the remote tool still forwards sound. Turn it off there. See [Fix echo and double audio](/guides/fix-echo-remote-desktop-meetings).
- *The sender page does not load:* port 7420 is not reachable from your device. Check the network first.

[Download Remote Visio for Mac](/download) or read [how it works](/how-it-works).

title: Use your phone as the microphone and webcam of a remote Mac
shortTitle: Your phone as mic and webcam
metaDescription: Use an iPhone or Android phone as the microphone, webcam and speaker of a Mac you control remotely, in web meetings, with nothing to install on the phone.
keywords: use phone as microphone for mac
use phone as microphone for remote mac
use phone as webcam for remote desktop
markdown:
Your phone can be the microphone, webcam and speaker of a Mac that is somewhere else, with no app to install on the phone. Remote Visio on the Mac serves a web page; you open it in the phone's browser, press **Start**, and web meetings on the Mac get your phone's microphone and camera, while the meeting's sound plays on your phone.

## When this is the right tool

- You control a Mac from far away (another room, the office, another city) through Parsec, AnyDesk, Screen Sharing or another remote desktop tool, and you take meetings on it.
- The device you sit at has no good microphone or camera, or your laptop's are in use, and your phone's are better.

If the phone and the Mac are **in the same room**, Apple's Continuity Camera and Continuity Microphone already do this for free, and you do not need Remote Visio.

## What you need

- On the Mac: Remote Visio ([download](/download)), and its [browser extension](/extension) in Chrome, Edge, Brave or Arc. Meetings run in that browser.
- On the phone: a browser. Safari on iPhone and Chrome on Android both work.
- A network path: the phone and the Mac on the same Wi-Fi, or both on [Tailscale](/guides/tailscale-setup-for-remote-visio) (it has iOS and Android apps).

## Step by step

1. **Find the Mac's address.** Click the Remote Visio icon in the Mac's menu bar: it lists addresses like `https://192.168.1.23:7420` (local network) or `https://100.101.102.103:7420` (Tailscale). Clicking one copies it.
2. **Open it on the phone.** Type the address in the phone's browser. Bookmark it, or add it to the home screen, for next time.
3. **Accept the certificate warning, once.** The browser warns that the certificate is not trusted. That is expected: browsers only give a page the microphone over HTTPS, and a tool on your own network cannot get a publicly trusted certificate, so Remote Visio makes its own. On iPhone, tap **Show Details**, then **visit this website**. In Chrome, tap **Advanced**, then **Proceed**.
4. **Press Start.** The browser asks for the microphone, then the camera. Allow both (or only the microphone, if you do not want to send video).
5. **On the Mac**, in Google Meet, Teams or Zoom on the web, choose **Remote Visio Microphone**, **Remote Visio Speaker** and **Remote Visio Camera**, and allow the site once.

The sender page now shows your camera's preview, a level meter that moves when you talk, and a green status for each device.

## The sender page, briefly

- **Three round buttons** over the preview turn the microphone, the camera and the speaker on and off at any time, without reconnecting. Red means off.
- **The pills** under the preview choose which microphone, speaker and camera of the phone to use. The names appear after the first Start.
- **Denoise, Clean and Raw** choose how much sound processing your browser applies. Denoise is a good default for a phone.
- **Statuses**: green when the device gets through and a meeting on the Mac uses it, amber while it is on its way or no meeting uses it yet, red with what to fix.

Every choice is remembered by that browser for next time.

## iPhone notes

- **Volume.** On iPhone and iPad a web page cannot set the volume, so there is no speaker slider: use the phone's volume buttons.
- **"Paused by the browser".** After a phone call, Siri, or some time in the background, iOS suspends the page's sound and nothing is sent. Tap the page or press a key to resume.
- **Keep the page in front.** A page in the background may be paused by the system. Keep the sender page open while you talk.

## Camera notes

- Remote Visio's camera travels as H.264. If the camera's status says *this browser cannot send H.264*, open the sender page in another browser on that device, such as Chrome.
- The camera reaches **web meetings** on the Mac through the browser extension. Builds that include the optional camera system extension also give video apps on the Mac a **Remote Visio Camera**, after a one-time approval in System Settings. See [A virtual camera for Google Meet](/guides/virtual-camera-chrome-extension-mac).
- Turning the camera off with its round button stops it (its light goes off); the microphone and speaker carry on.

## Use headphones or the speaker?

Either. While the sender page's speaker is on, your browser's echo cancellation is on too, so the meeting's sound from the phone's speaker is not sent back into the meeting. Turn off sound in your remote desktop tool, or you will hear the meeting twice. Details in [Fix echo and double audio](/guides/fix-echo-remote-desktop-meetings).

## Limits

- The microphone and speaker are for **web meetings in a Chromium browser** on the Mac. The Zoom, Teams and FaceTime apps cannot use them: [join from the browser](/guides/join-zoom-teams-from-browser-on-mac).
- There is no pairing code: anyone who can reach port 7420 on the Mac can connect. Use networks you trust.

[Download Remote Visio for Mac](/download) and give it a try with the phone in your pocket.

title: Join Zoom and Teams from the browser on a remote Mac
shortTitle: Zoom and Teams in the browser
metaDescription: Remote Visio's microphone and speaker work in web meetings. How to join Zoom and Microsoft Teams from the browser on a remote Mac, and pick the right devices.
keywords: zoom web client microphone remote mac
markdown:
Remote Visio's microphone and speaker exist inside web pages of a Chromium browser on the Mac, so the meeting has to run in that browser, not in the Zoom or Teams app. Both services let you join from the browser: Zoom with **Join from your browser**, Teams with **Continue on this browser**. Google Meet runs in the browser anyway. Then pick Remote Visio's devices in the meeting's settings.

## Why the apps cannot see Remote Visio's microphone

Remote Visio does not install an audio driver on the Mac. Its browser extension adds **Remote Visio Microphone**, **Remote Visio Speaker** and **Remote Visio Camera** to the list of devices a web page sees. That keeps installation simple (no administrator, no System Settings approval for the extension) and leaves the Mac's own sound alone. The trade-off: native apps never see those devices. That includes the Zoom, Teams and FaceTime apps, macOS dictation, and Safari and Firefox, which cannot load the extension.

The camera is the exception: builds that include the optional Remote Visio Camera system extension give native video apps a virtual camera, after a one-time approval.

## Before you start

- Remote Visio is running on the Mac, with its [extension](/extension) installed in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Vivaldi or Opera.
- The sender page is open and started on your device (see [Use your microphone on a remote Mac](/guides/use-microphone-on-remote-mac)).
- Meeting pages that were open before you installed the extension have been reloaded.

## Zoom: join from your browser

1. Open the meeting link in the Chromium browser on the Mac.
2. When the page offers to open the Zoom app, cancel, and choose **Join from your browser**. (If the link opens the app straight away, copy the link into the browser instead.)
3. In the meeting, use the small arrows next to **Mute** and **Start Video**: choose **Remote Visio Microphone** and **Remote Visio Speaker** under the microphone's arrow, and **Remote Visio Camera** under the video's.
4. When the extension asks whether the site may use Remote Visio's devices, click **Allow**.

## Microsoft Teams: continue on this browser

1. Open the meeting link in the Chromium browser on the Mac.
2. On the page that offers the Teams app, choose **Continue on this browser**.
3. Before joining, or during the meeting in **Settings → Devices**, set the microphone to Remote Visio Microphone, the speaker to Remote Visio Speaker and the camera to Remote Visio Camera.
4. Allow the site when the extension asks.

## Google Meet

Meet runs in the browser. In the meeting, open **Settings**: **Audio** holds the microphone and speakers, **Video** the camera. Choose the three Remote Visio devices and allow the site once.

## Other web meetings

Any web page that lets you choose a microphone, speaker or camera lists Remote Visio's devices: Jitsi and Whereby, for example. The extension asks once per site, the one in the address bar, with one question for the three devices, and remembers the answer.

## Let Remote Visio be the default

The extension's button has a switch called **Use Remote Visio by default**, on unless you turn it off. With it on:

- a site that asks for *any* microphone or camera, without naming one, gets Remote Visio's (after the same one-time question);
- on a site you allowed, what the page plays on the default output goes to Remote Visio Speaker, but only while your sending device listens; otherwise it plays on the Mac as usual.

A site that remembered one of the Mac's own devices by name (say, "MacBook Pro Microphone") keeps getting that one: pick Remote Visio's once in its settings.

## Checking that it works

- On your sending device, the microphone's status says *Sending · used by 1 page on the Mac* and the speaker's says *Playing the meeting's sound*.
- On the Mac, the extension's button shows each device with the site using it.
- The meeting's own microphone meter moves when you talk.

If the meeting hears nothing, check in this order: the sender page is started and its microphone button is not red; the meeting uses Remote Visio Microphone; the site is not listed as **Blocked** in the extension's button (remove it, and it asks again); the page was reloaded after the extension was installed.

## Turn off the remote desktop tool's sound

Remote Visio sends the meeting's sound to your device. If your remote tool also forwards the Mac's sound, you hear everything twice. Turn sound off in the remote tool. More in [Fix echo and double audio](/guides/fix-echo-remote-desktop-meetings).

[Download Remote Visio for Mac](/download) to get started.

title: Tailscale for Remote Visio: reach your Mac from anywhere
metaDescription: Remote Visio needs your device to reach port 7420 on the Mac. Tailscale makes that work from anywhere for free. Setup, addresses, and the security note.
markdown:
Remote Visio needs one thing from the network: the device in front of you must reach port 7420 on the Mac. On the same local network that just works. From anywhere else, the simplest way is Tailscale, which is free for personal use: install it on both devices, sign in with the same account, and open `https://<the Mac's 100.x address>:7420`.

## Why port 7420 has to be reachable

Remote Visio has no server of its own in the middle. Your browser talks to the Mac directly, in two steps:

1. **Signalling.** The browser loads the sender page from the Mac at `https://<mac>:7420` and exchanges the connection details with it. This needs port 7420 to be reachable from your device. It is the step people miss.
2. **Media.** Your microphone, camera and the meeting's sound then travel over an encrypted WebRTC connection, directly between the two devices when possible.

Across the open internet, the first step is the hard one. Many home connections have no public address of their own (carrier-grade NAT), so port forwarding cannot help. Tailscale solves both steps at once.

## What Tailscale does here

Tailscale builds a private network, a *tailnet*, between your devices. Each one gets a stable address of the form `100.x.x.x`, and devices in the same tailnet can reach each other on any port, wherever they are. Port 7420 on the Mac becomes reachable from your laptop or phone, and WebRTC connects inside that network, usually directly. It is also how Remote Visio's author runs it.

## Setup

1. **Install Tailscale on the Mac.** Download it from [tailscale.com/download](https://tailscale.com/download) (or `brew install --cask tailscale`), open it and sign in.
2. **Install Tailscale on your device**: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS or Android. Sign in **with the same account**.
3. **Find the Mac's address.** The Remote Visio icon in the Mac's menu bar lists its sender addresses: pick the one that starts with `100.`. In Terminal, `tailscale ip -4` prints it too.
4. **Check the path.** From your device, the Tailscale app shows the Mac as connected. (Advanced: `tailscale ping <the Mac's 100.x address>` says whether the path is direct or relayed.)
5. **Open the sender page**: `https://100.x.x.x:7420`, with the Mac's address. Accept the certificate warning once and press **Start**.

Then pick Remote Visio's devices in the meeting on the Mac, as in [the main guide](/guides/use-microphone-on-remote-mac).

Bookmark the address: it stays the same. If you have several Macs with Remote Visio in your tailnet, the sender page can find the others too, and its **Connection** section lists each one.

## Same local network: no Tailscale needed

If your device and the Mac are on the same network (home or office Wi-Fi), use the Mac's local address instead, such as `https://192.168.1.23:7420`. The menu-bar menu lists it. If they are in the same room, though, think twice: an iPhone next to the Mac can already be its microphone through Apple's Continuity Microphone.

## Without Tailscale, over the open internet

It is possible, and harder:

- the Mac's port 7420 must be reachable from the internet, with port forwarding and a stable or dynamic hostname, which carrier-grade NAT rules out;
- some networks will refuse a direct WebRTC connection, and then you need a TURN relay that you run or rent yourself. Remote Visio's receiver takes one with its `-turn`, `-turn-user` and `-turn-pass` options ([SETUP.md](https://github.com/ohayak/relaymic/blob/master/SETUP.md) explains them).

Exposing port 7420 to the internet is also a security risk, see below. For most people, Tailscale is the better answer.

## Security: keep port 7420 inside networks you trust

In this version, Remote Visio has **no password and no pairing code**. Anyone who can reach port 7420 on your Mac, including a web page open on a device that can reach it, can open the sender page and connect as the sender, and the sender hears what meeting pages play into Remote Visio Speaker. So:

- keep the Mac reachable only inside your tailnet or a local network you trust;
- do not forward port 7420 on your router;
- remember that everyone in a shared tailnet can reach it.

Inside a tailnet, only devices you have signed in can connect, and the traffic is encrypted twice: by Tailscale, and by WebRTC itself.

## Troubleshooting

- **The sender page does not load.** That is the signalling step: the device cannot reach port 7420. Check that both devices show as connected in Tailscale, and that you used the Mac's `100.` address.
- **The page loads, then stays on "Connecting...".** Signalling works and media does not. That is rare inside Tailscale. Open the sender page with `?debug=1`, press Start, wait 15 seconds and copy the log: it shows the connection attempts. A network that drops UDP (a VPN, a firewall, Wi-Fi client isolation) is the usual cause.
- **Choppy audio.** Loss on the network between the two devices. `tailscale ping` tells you whether the path is direct or relayed; a direct path is better.

Next: [download Remote Visio](/download) and [add the extension](/extension).

title: Fix echo and double audio in meetings over remote desktop
metaDescription: Hearing the meeting twice, your own voice or an echo in meetings on a remote Mac? The causes, and the fix for each one, with Remote Visio.
keywords: hear meeting audio twice remote desktop
hear my own voice remote desktop
markdown:
When you take a meeting on a remote Mac, sound can reach you by two roads: your remote desktop tool's audio, and Remote Visio. Most echo and double-audio problems come from both roads being open at once. The fix is almost always the same: **turn sound off in the remote desktop tool, and keep the sender page's speaker on.**

## Symptom 1: you hear the meeting twice

**What it sounds like:** every voice arrives twice, a fraction of a second apart.

**Why:** Remote Visio sends what the meeting plays into Remote Visio Speaker to your device. Your remote desktop tool also forwards the Mac's sound. They have different delays, so you get two copies.

**Fix:** turn off sound transmission in your remote desktop tool's settings. Remote Visio carries the meeting's sound now, on its own low-latency connection.

## Symptom 2: you hear your own voice

**What it sounds like:** you talk, and a moment later you hear yourself.

**Why:** the remote tool is still forwarding audio, and some tools even send the Mac's *input* back to you.

**Fix:** the same: turn the remote tool's audio off.

## Symptom 3: the other participants hear an echo of themselves

**What it sounds like:** people in the meeting complain that they hear their own voice back.

**Why:** the meeting's sound comes out of your speakers and goes back into your microphone. Your browser can cancel that, but only when it knows what is playing. On the sender page, **echo cancellation is on while the page's speaker is on**. If you turned the page's speaker off and listen to the meeting through the remote desktop tool instead, the browser has nothing to cancel, and your microphone picks up the meeting.

**Fix, one of:**

- turn the sender page's speaker **on** and the remote tool's audio **off**, so the meeting plays through the page and echo cancellation kicks in; or
- wear headphones.

## Symptom 4: the meeting hears the room around the Mac

**What it sounds like:** people hear a TV, an office, typing, in the room where the Mac stands.

**Why:** the meeting uses one of the Mac's own microphones, not Remote Visio Microphone.

**Fix:** in the meeting's audio settings, choose **Remote Visio Microphone**. To be sure the room stays out of every app and page, use the menu-bar menu: **Controls → Mute This Mac's Microphone**. It mutes the Mac's built-in, USB and Bluetooth microphones while Remote Visio runs and puts them back when it stops. **Mute This Mac's Speakers** keeps the room quiet the other way.

## Symptom 5: choppy or robotic audio

**Why:** packets lost or delayed on the network between your device and the Mac. Remote Visio passes your audio through without decoding it on the Mac, and the Mac's browser sizes its jitter buffer to the network by itself, so there is nothing to tune on the Mac.

**What helps:**

- a direct path between the devices. With Tailscale, `tailscale ping <the Mac's 100.x address>` says whether the path is direct or relayed;
- a better network on the sending side: Wi-Fi close to the router, or a cable;
- the receiver's log, which records the packets received and lost every 10 seconds while you talk. The [support page](/support) says where to find it.

## Symptom 6: the first syllable of quiet words disappears

**Why:** silence suppression (DTX) skips what it takes for silence, and it clips the start of softly spoken words.

**Fix:** leave DTX off. It is off by default in Remote Visio; it only turns on if the receiver is started with the `-dtx` option.

## Symptom 7: you hear nothing from the meeting

Check, in order:

1. The sender page's **speaker button** is not red. Red means off: the meeting is muted on your device only.
2. The speaker's status. *Playing the meeting's sound* means it arrives; check your device's own volume and the speaker's slider. *No meeting uses Remote Visio Speaker yet* means the meeting plays somewhere else: choose Remote Visio Speaker in its settings.
3. The meeting runs in a Chromium browser on the Mac. The Zoom and Teams apps cannot use Remote Visio Speaker: [join from the browser](/guides/join-zoom-teams-from-browser-on-mac).

## A good setup, in short

- Remote desktop tool: screen, keyboard, mouse. **Sound off.**
- Remote Visio sender page: microphone on, **speaker on**, Denoise for most rooms.
- Meeting on the Mac: Remote Visio Microphone, Remote Visio Speaker, Remote Visio Camera, from the [browser extension](/extension).
- Optional: Mute This Mac's Microphone and Speakers, if the Mac shares a room with people.

New to Remote Visio? Start with [how it works](/how-it-works) or [download it for Mac](/download).

title: A virtual camera for Google Meet on a Mac, no admin rights
shortTitle: A virtual camera without admin rights
metaDescription: A virtual camera for Google Meet, Teams and Zoom on the web, fed by your phone or laptop: no administrator, no System Settings approval.
keywords: virtual camera chrome extension google meet
markdown:
Remote Visio can bring the camera of the device in front of you (a phone, a laptop) to a Mac you control remotely, as a webcam called **Remote Visio Camera**: a webcam for remote desktop, which your remote desktop tool cannot pass through to a Mac by itself. For web meetings in a Chromium browser, it comes from a browser extension, which needs no administrator and no approval in System Settings. That makes it work on many company-managed Macs where installing a classic virtual camera is blocked.

## Two ways to be a camera on a Mac

Remote Visio has two cameras with the same name, for two kinds of apps:

| What differs | Browser extension camera | Camera system extension |
|---|---|---|
| Who sees it | Web pages in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Vivaldi, Opera | Video apps on the Mac (Zoom, FaceTime, OBS…) and web pages |
| Installation | Add the extension from the Chrome Web Store | Included only in builds that carry it; activated by the app |
| Approval | None | A one-time approval in System Settings |
| Managed Macs | Usually works | The management policy may block it |

Both are fed by the same video, so either one shows your remote camera.

## How the browser extension's camera works

The **Remote Visio Camera** extension (its Chrome Web Store name, from when it carried only the camera) adds three devices to the lists that web pages see: Remote Visio Camera, Remote Visio Microphone and Remote Visio Speaker. Your sending device's camera reaches the Remote Visio app on the Mac over an encrypted WebRTC connection, as H.264. The app passes the video to the meeting page over a connection inside the Mac, without decoding it, and the browser decodes it like any webcam's.

Nothing on that last leg leaves the Mac, and a site gets the camera only after you allow it, once per site.

## Set it up

1. **Install Remote Visio on the Mac** ([download](/download)) and add the extension from the menu-bar menu: **Install Browser Extension…**, then **Add to Chrome** on the store page. Pin it so its button stays in the toolbar.
2. **Start the sender page** on your phone or laptop (`https://<the Mac's address>:7420`) and allow the camera. The camera is sent unless you turn it off with its round button.
3. **In Google Meet**, open **Settings → Video** and choose **Remote Visio Camera**. In Teams on the web, **Settings → Devices**. In Zoom on the web, the arrow next to **Start Video**.
4. **Allow the site** when the extension asks. One question covers the camera, the microphone and the speaker.

Until video arrives, the camera shows a dark card titled "Remote Visio Camera" whose second line says what it is waiting for, for example the sending device.

## On a company-managed Mac

Organizations often manage Macs with a device management (MDM) policy that only allows system extensions they list. On such a Mac:

- **The browser extension's camera works without asking anyone**, unless the organization also manages the browser and forbids the extension. In that case, Remote Visio's **Install Browser Extension…** says so, names what IT would have to allow (for a store extension, usually its ID, `bhijcffjnmjijifjiaeibbogmbohdmon`), and offers other Chromium browsers you have.
- **The camera system extension may be refused.** The menu-bar menu then says the camera failed because of the Mac's management policy. Nothing on the Mac can override that. To use it, ask whoever manages the Mac to allow team ID `99F33YCKX9`, bundle `com.remotevisio.app.camera` (a Camera / Core Media I/O extension). For web meetings you can simply skip it.

## Things that look wrong but are fine

- **Two cameras named "Remote Visio Camera".** When the system extension is active, web pages list both: the system extension's and the browser extension's. Both show your remote camera. Pick either.
- **A dark card instead of video.** The camera is waiting: on the sending device, the camera's round button must be on (not red), and its status says why nothing is sent.

## Requirements and limits

- The sending browser must be able to send **H.264**. If the camera's status says *this browser cannot send H.264*, use another browser on that device, such as Chrome.
- The browser extension's camera works in **Chromium browsers** (version 111 or later), not in Safari or Firefox.
- The extension works in the **browser profile** it was added to. Private windows get it only once you turn on **Allow in Incognito** in the extension's details.
- Native apps (the Zoom, Teams and FaceTime apps) see only the system extension's camera, where it is installed and approved. Their **microphone** cannot come from Remote Visio at all: [join from the browser](/guides/join-zoom-teams-from-browser-on-mac).

More about the extension, including each permission it asks for, on [the extension page](/extension). [Download Remote Visio for Mac](/download).
